summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with morbid obesity was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema over several weeks, along with symptoms of polyuria and polydipsia. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 11.6) and acute decompensated systolic heart failure (LVEF 30%) on presentation. Initial evaluation revealed atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction, which was suspected to be the cause of tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy. Despite successful cardioversion, the rhythm recurred, leading to a successful catheter ablation on hospital day 16. He was aggressively diuresed with IV furosemide and metolazone, losing approximately 80 pounds, and was transitioned to oral heart failure medications including lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. Insulin therapy was initiated and titrated for diabetes management. He developed transient acute kidney injury likely due to contrast and diuresis. A fungal rash under the pannus was treated with topical miconazole. Sleep apnea was suspected due to nocturnal apneic episodes, prompting an outpatient sleep study referral. He was discharged home in sinus rhythm on warfarin with Lovenox bridge, with follow-up arranged in cardiology, electrophysiology, heart failure, and diabetes clinics.
